entry.title: System Design (Part-1)
entry.summary:
What is System Design?
The Big Picture
Imagine you're building WhatsApp from scratch. You start with a simple chat app that works for 10 users. But what happens when: 1 million users join?
Users send photos and videos?
People in India want to chat with people in the US?
Your server crashes?
System design is about solving these "scale problems" - building systems that work reliably for millions of users across the globe. 1995: Amazon was a simple website selling books from Jeff Bezos's garage One server Simple database Few hundred customers 2025: Amazon handles: Millions of products Hundreds of millions of customers Black Friday traffic spikes Global operations in 200+ countries System design is the journey from garage to global scale. High Level Design (HLD)
It describes the main component that would be developed for resulting products. Focusing on the macro-level structure and the interaction between major components. Low Level Design (LLD)
It describes the design of each element mentioned in the HLD system. Focusing on the micro-level design of each individual module.
